title: fix: use available defaults for Polli harnesses
author: g33ky00
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #15753
Fixes #15717

- Use an available tool-calling model by default in Hermes, DSH, Pi and Prime.
- Keep harness validation on the id field returned by /v1/models. The separate /models endpoint uses name.
- Verified against the live catalog; 246 CLI tests and build pass.

gist.headline: Four harnesses find their footing
gist.blurb: Hermes, DSH, Pi, and Prime now start with a model that’s actually in the catalog and can call tools. A surprisingly useful quality in a default.
gist.summary: Updated the default models for the Hermes, DSH, Pi, and Prime Polli CLI harnesses to available tool-calling models while keeping validation against the id field returned by /v1/models.
gist.impact: Polli CLI users can start those four harnesses with working defaults, and model validation continues to match the /v1/models catalog.
gist.visual_concept: Polli CLI is represented by a cozy retro terminal, not a separate mascot. Polli checks four labeled harness stations—Hermes, DSH, Pi, and Prime—each connected to a tool-calling model in a small catalog; nearby code-plants make the workspace feel like a garden.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel art garden workspace, four little retro terminals labeled Hermes, DSH, Pi, and Prime glow lime green (#ecf874) as Polli checks their connections to a shared model catalog beside sprouting code-plants. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears tiny tool-belt, stays small-to-medium within the scene, and is strictly pixel art, never realistic. Cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes, chunky sprites, warm cream background, dark purple (#110518) outlines, nostalgic but beautiful and emotionally warm.
